PTC.thesis_one_line: Pending takeover: Schneider Electric signed a definitive agreement on 4 Oct 2026 to buy PTC for $205 cash (42.3% premium); the stock ($192.59 on 5 Oct) is now a capped merger-arbitrage position, out of mandate; the PLM/CAD franchise facts (ARR +9.1% cc ex-divested) are unchanged.
kill_criteria: Event: HSR second request or CFIUS review that pushes closing past the 4 Apr 2027 Initial End Date (auto-extends to 4 Jan 2028 at most).
Event: spread to $205 widens above about 15% (price below about $178) without news.
Event: Schneider's equity raise (ABO) fails, its A-category credit rating is put at risk, or the $25bn bridge terms change.
Event: termination notice, or the $700m PTC termination fee is triggered (superior proposal or recommendation change).
Event: a competing proposal appears (reopens standalone valuation).

Original operating criteria are moot while the merger agreement is pending and are re-applied only if the deal terminates: Constant-currency ARR growth (ex-divested businesses) falls below 6% YoY for two consecutive quarters. | Consolidated net debt (LT debt less cash, per 10-Q balance sheet) rises above $2.0B without a corresponding step-up in FY run-rate FCF guidance. | FY guidance is cut (not just reaffirmed/raised) in any quarterly release. | Non-GAAP operating margin (currently guided ~41%) compresses below 36% for two consecutive quarters. | Any 8-K disclosure of a material cybersecurity incident, restatement, or auditor change (none identified as of this review).
key_adverse_facts: Q1'26 GAAP EPS of $4.98 includes a one-time $463M pre-tax gain on the Kepware/ThingWorx sale; GAAP EPS is not comparable across quarters this fiscal year.
As-reported revenue is guided down 2% to flat for FY26 due to lapping the divested businesses, which will keep creating headline optics that look like decline even though ARR is growing.
Long-term debt rose from $1,172.7M (2025-12-31) to $1,398.2M (2026-06-30), partly to fund an outsized $525M Q3'26 buyback.
Share-based compensation and Form 4 insider-selling patterns were not reviewed this pass (time-boxed gap).

Definitive merger agreement dated 4 Oct 2026 (8-K Item 1.01, filed 5 Oct 2026): $205 cash, close targeted by Q3 2027, subject to PTC shareholder vote, HSR and CFIUS; $700m termination fee payable by PTC; no reverse termination fee found.
At $192.59 the gross spread to $205 is $12.41 (6.4%) against about -25% to the undisturbed $144.03 if the deal fails (market-implied completion probability about 80%).
data_conflicts: b1 composite ranks PTC only decile 5/10 (live_rank 290) because GAAP-based momentum/ebit_ev sub-factors are depressed by the Q2'26 divestiture accounting; the underlying ARR/quality trend is stronger than the composite implies.
PTC.horizon: Event-driven to deal close (Schneider guides Q3 2027; agreement outside date 4 Apr 2027, extendable to 4 Jan 2028); not a 12-36 month compounding holding
PTC.confidence_in_thesis: medium (guidance has been raised twice consecutively and ARR growth beat its own range, but the FY26 GAAP EPS is contaminated by a one-time gain and revenue optics will remain confusing for a few more quarters, which could delay re-rating)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Re-assessed 5 Oct 2026 (RA1). 10-year FCF/share reverse DCF (terminal 3.5%, FY26 FCF guide $850M / 110.7M shares, 10% discount rate = 10-yr Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep 2026 + beta 1.1 x ERP 4.5-5%): $138.12 implied 5.1%/yr, $144.03 5.7%, $192.59 9.6%, $205 10.4% (SBC-burdened 14.1% and 14.9% at the last two); at a 9% rate 2.9%, 3.5%, 7.2%, 8.0%. Base case 7-8%/yr, so at $192.59 the price implies growth above base. The price is anchored by the $205 offer, so this is not a standalone valuation.

PTC.scenario_basis: Annualised from $192.59 (5 Oct 2026). Base: deal closes at $205 about Sep 2027, cash at 3.75% for the remaining two years. Bull: closes by about Apr 2027 (faster close; no competing-bid scenario assumed). Bear: deal fails at about month 12 on CFIUS/HSR/vote/financing, stock back to about $135, then 7%/yr standalone growth. Own arithmetic.

ROP.thesis_one_line: Diversified vertical-market software conglomerate at a rare discount to its own history, but now funding buybacks with a lot more debt than before.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt / annualized adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.5x (currently ~3.1x) without a corresponding acceleration in adjusted FCF growth.
Adjusted DEPS guidance is cut (not just reaffirmed/raised) in any quarterly release.
Organic revenue growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters (currently guided ~6%).
Any credit-rating downgrade action tied to the debt-funded buyback program.
A material adverse resolution or write-down of the residual Indicor minority stake.
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated long-term debt grew from $6,457.0M (2025-03-31) to $10,601.1M (2026-06-30), a 64% increase in five quarters, largely to fund buybacks.
Net debt / annualized adjusted EBITDA is now approximately 3.1x, up materially from Roper's historically much lower leverage.

GAAP EPS ($11.62 in Q2'26) is dominated by a volatile, non-cash fair-value gain on the Indicor minority investment and is not usable for trend analysis; only adjusted DEPS ($5.38 in Q2'26) is comparable.
Indicor's pending divestiture of its instrumentation businesses is an unresolved complexity whose proceeds/timing are explicitly excluded from Roper's own guidance.
data_conflicts: b1's momentum and SUE percentiles for ROP are weak (~0.20 each) partly because they are computed on GAAP EPS, which has become highly noisy since the Indicor minority stake began being marked to fair value; this understates the underlying adjusted-earnings trend.
ROP.confidence_in_thesis: medium (valuation discount and recurring-revenue quality are genuine and durable, but the sharp rise in debt-funded buybacks is a real change in capital-allocation character that this dossier could not fully resolve in one pass)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No ROP row exists in v1_valuation_table.csv, so there is no systematic model to reconcile against; this agent's own reverse-DCF implies ~2.3%/yr perpetual growth priced in at $358.56 (16.1x NTM adjusted P/E), versus a base case of 7-9%/yr adjusted FCF-per-share growth, so implied growth is below base case, supporting a cheap view, tempered by the leverage reservation.

ROP.scenario_basis: Starting point: FY26 adjusted DEPS guide midpoint $22.225 on $358.56 price (16.1x P/E); bear = leverage concerns cause multiple compression to 13x alongside organic growth slowing to ~3%; base = adjusted DEPS compounds ~8%/yr (organic ~5-6% plus bolt-on M&A) with multiple flat to modestly higher toward 17-18x; bull = deleveraging post-Indicor-instrumentation-sale plus continued 8%+ adjusted DEPS growth re-rates the multiple toward 20x; no meaningful dividend yield in any case.

STZ.thesis_one_line: America's top-selling imported-beer maker (Modelo, Corona) at a cheap multiple as depletions stabilize, clouded by an unresolved securities lawsuit and a CEO transition.
kill_criteria: Beer depletions turn negative by more than -2% YoY for two consecutive quarters, reopening the FY26-style demand shock.
An adverse ruling or settlement in the Meza securities class action that results in a disclosed material liability or admission.
Consolidated net debt/comparable EBITDA rises above 3.5x (target/current ~3.0x).
FY2027 comparable EPS guidance ($11.20-$11.90) is cut in any subsequent quarterly release.
The disclosed CEO transition results in a strategy change materially deviating from the current beer-first capital-allocation priorities.
key_adverse_facts: Active federal securities class action (Meza v. Constellation Brands, W.D.N.Y. 6:25-cv-6107) alleging misleading statements about the beer business; motion to dismiss argued July 22, 2026 with no ruling found in filings reviewed.
Related derivative suits (Silva, Mason, Wasserman) consolidated/stayed pending the Meza outcome.

10-Q explicitly lists a President/CEO transition as a named forward-looking risk factor; current signer of the Q1 FY2028 release is a different CEO than the one named as a Meza defendant, and this dossier could not fully verify the current governance status this pass.

Beer depletions, while much improved (-0.3% in the latest quarter vs -4% to -2% a year earlier), are still negative, and remain exposed to Hispanic-consumer-spending and immigration-enforcement dynamics outside management's control.
data_conflicts: b1's factor row for STZ is marked insufficient_families_no_composite (Value/Momentum/SUE families are blank), so the pre-registered quant model has no real opinion on this name; its advancement rested on qualitative triage and price data, not a cross-validated composite.
STZ.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium (the beer-demand stabilization and cheap valuation are real and evidence-based, but the unresolved securities litigation and CEO-transition risk factor are genuine, unquantifiable overhangs that were not fully resolved in this pass)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No STZ row exists in v1_valuation_table.csv, so there is no systematic model to reconcile against; this agent's own reverse-DCF implies roughly -0.4%/yr perpetual growth priced in at $113.63 (9.8x NTM comparable P/E), below this agent's 0-2%/yr base case (which itself is close to management's own FY2027 guide of -1% to +1% organic growth), so implied growth is at/below base case even though the litigation and CEO-transition overhangs keep the verdict at INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE.

STZ.scenario_basis: Starting point: FY2027 comparable EPS guide midpoint $11.55 on ~$19.6B approximate market cap (9.8x P/E, ~8.4% approximate FCF yield); bear = adverse Meza ruling plus renewed beer-depletion declines (back toward -3%/yr) and multiple compression to ~7x; base = depletions stabilize near flat (0-2%/yr) with multiple holding near 10x plus the ~3.7% dividend yield; bull = beer share gains resume, wine-and-spirits turnaround adds growth, and litigation is dismissed, re-rating the multiple toward 12-13x.
